findings.issue: Simple cooldown timer - no performance concerns
findings.description: Decrements a float timer when > 0. Minimal CPU cost.
Early return if queue empty, spawns max 1 card per frame. Well optimized.

findings.issue: Dictionary.Clear() called every frame may cause GC pressure
findings.description: Lines 161-162 clear _actionJustPressed and _actionJustReleased dictionaries every frame. If these have capacity, Clear() doesn't release memory, so GC impact is minimal.
findings.recommendation: Consider pooling or fixed-size arrays if profiling shows allocations. Input.GetActionStrength() calls are acceptable for polling.

findings.description: Line 250: `var gravity = ProjectSettings.GetSetting("physics/3d/default_gravity").AsSingle();` performs a string lookup in ProjectSettings dictionary every physics frame (60 Hz). This is a static value that should be cached in _Ready().
findings.recommendation: Add private field `private float _gravity;` and cache in _Ready(): `_gravity = ProjectSettings.GetSetting("physics/3d/default_gravity").AsSingle();`. Then use _gravity instead of querying every frame.

findings.description: Lines 235-236 call GetActionStrength 4 times for directional input. While not expensive individually, this is repeated every physics frame.
findings.recommendation: InputService already provides MovementInput property (line 29). Consider using that instead if InputService is accessible, or cache results if multiple systems need the same input.

findings.issue: Physics raycast performed every physics frame (60 Hz)
findings.description: DetectInteractable() at line 68 calls PerformRaycast() (lines 81-98) which uses DirectSpaceState.IntersectRay every physics frame. Raycasting is expensive. Additionally, FindInteractableInHierarchy (lines 100-111) traverses parent chain for every hit.
findings.recommendation: Reduce raycast frequency to 20-30 Hz using a timer/counter (e.g., only raycast every 2-3 physics frames). Interaction detection doesn't need 60 Hz precision. Alternatively, use frame skipping: `if (_frameCounter++ % 2 != 0) return;`
findings.estimated_savings: ~0.05-0.2ms per frame when reduced to 30 Hz (50% reduction)

findings.issue: List.RemoveAt() called in backwards iteration loop
findings.description: Line 71: `_onBelt.RemoveAt(i);` inside backwards for loop (line 66). While backwards iteration avoids index shifting issues, RemoveAt still has O(n) cost. With many cards on belt, this compounds.
findings.recommendation: Use swap-remove pattern: swap element with last, then RemoveAt(Count-1) for O(1) removal. Or collect indices to remove and batch remove afterward.
findings.estimated_savings: ~0.01-0.05ms per frame with 10+ cards on belt

findings.issue: Linear velocity set every frame for all cards on belt
findings.description: Line 84: `card.LinearVelocity = dir.Normalized() * Speed;` recalculates and sets velocity for all cards every physics frame. While necessary for conveyor behavior, Normalized() creates vector allocations.
findings.recommendation: If direction is constant (straight belt), cache the normalized direction vector. If belt curves, this is unavoidable.

findings.description: Delegates physics to _physicsComponents list via foreach. This is appropriate component architecture.
findings.recommendation: No action needed. Pattern is correct.

findings.issue: Drop preview update every physics frame
findings.description: Line 96 calls CardDropper.UpdateDropPreview() every physics frame when preparing drop. Depends on implementation complexity.
findings.recommendation: Audit CardDropper.UpdateDropPreview() implementation for expensive operations (raycasts, GetNode calls, etc.). Consider reducing update frequency to 30 Hz if expensive.

findings.issue: Distance calculation performed every frame in IsTargetInRange
findings.description: Line 138: `Camera.GlobalPosition.DistanceTo(target.InteractionBody.GlobalPosition)` called every frame when target exists. DistanceTo involves sqrt operation.
findings.recommendation: Use DistanceSquaredTo and compare squared distances (avoid sqrt). Only relevant if target changes frequently.

CRITICAL: Reduce InteractionSystem raycast frequency from 60 Hz to 20-30 Hz using frame skipping
Optimize ConveyorBelt RemoveAt() with swap-remove pattern
